title: Dawn probe scribble — quick regression + ad-hoc rubric
content:
Purpose:
- Quick personal scratchpad for a morning pass on the "dawn" workload (low-latency chat with short instructions, heavy few-shot).
- Build a tiny ad-hoc rubric I can reuse for fast triage and hand off to Mira if needed.

Context / motivation:
- After v2.0.0 rollout (canary traffic yesterday) some partners reported higher succinctness and occasional dropped clauses in multi-step outputs. Suspect sampler/tokenizer interaction + KV-cache alignment change (INFR-3245).
- This doc is grainy: notes, sample evidence, quick scoring, and immediate triage items. Not polished.

Hypotheses to test quickly:
1) Truncation at exact token boundary due to tokenization change -> mid-sentence cutoff more frequent.
2) KV-cache miss at small batch sizes when context reuse expected -> repeated phrases or reset-like behavior.
3) Temperature/sampling schedule default drift (config fallback) -> shorter outputs with higher repetition.

Ad-hoc rubric (single-pass, 1–4 where 4=good):
- Coherence (1-4): Does the answer follow prompt steps and keep necessary context?
- Completeness (1-4): Does it return all required items (e.g., list of 3 actions)?
- Stability (1-4): Repeatability across 3 seeds (low variance = higher score).
- Hallucination (1-4): Factual inventing or unsupported claims (lower is worse).
- Overall pass (yes/no) threshold: mean >= 3.0 and no category <= 2

Quick sample set (short prompts to reproduce behavior):
P1 (instructional, few-shot):
- "You are an assistant. Given a short customer message, return (1) one-sentence summary, (2) suggested next action (one of escalate/reply-with-steps/ask-clarifying-question), (3) three bullet points to include in reply."
Context examples provided: 2 shot.

Observed outputs (v1.9.2 baseline vs v2.0.0 canary):
- Baseline (v1.9.2) seed A:
  Summary: Customer cannot log in after password reset; sees 403 on POST.
  Action: escalate
  Bullets:
    - Confirm account id and timestamp of reset
    - Check auth service logs for 403 code
    - Provide temporary recovery link
- Canary (v2.0.0) seed A:
  Summary: Customer can't log in after password reset.
  Action: escalate
  Bullets:
    - Confirm account id
    - Check auth logs
  <-- note: third bullet missing, trailing ellipsis (cut off mid-thought)

- Canary seed B (same prompt, different seed):
  Summary: Customer unable to log in after password reset; receives an HTTP 403 on attempt to POST credentials.
  Action: reply-with-steps
  Bullets:
    - Ask for exact timestamp and device
    - Suggest trying incognito
    - If still failing, escalate to SRE
  <-- different selected action and more complete bullets

Quick scored notes for P1 (single-pass):
- Baseline mean scores: Coherence 4, Completeness 4, Stability 4, Hallucination 4, Mean 4 -> pass
- Canary observed: seed A: Coherence 2 (cutoff), Completeness 2, Stability 2, Hallucination 4 -> mean 2.5 -> FAIL
                 seed B: Coherence 3, Completeness 3, Stability 3, Hallucination 4 -> mean 3.25 -> PASS
- Interpretation: non-deterministic regression tied to seed + possibly batch/timing.

P2 (longer context boundary test):
- Prompt contains a user conversation of ~1.1k tokens (3 messages, some metadata), ask assistant to extract 5 action items and reorder by priority. Expected stable ordering and 5 items.

Observed (canary): often returns 4 items; sometimes returns 6 with duplicated items. Baseline always 5. Scored: Baseline mean 4 across categories, Canary mean ~2.8 (drop primarily in completeness and stability).

Quick diagnostic steps tried locally (notes):
- Replayed requests with identical request metadata -> variability remains across seeds.
- Instrumented tokenization for P1: found rare off-by-1 token counts when multi-byte unicode present in examples (emoji in a sample message).
- KV-cache trace (light): observed cache flush events aligned with very short inter-request gaps when using connection pooling and reusing contextIDs. Suspect timing/GC race.
- Sampling params: default temperature fallback was 0.6 in canary instead of 0.7 (PR #1420 changed default in some paths) — small but could shift action classification.

Immediate mitigations (fast):
- Pin tokenizer version in canary config for the dawn route to v1.2.1 (rollback) to validate hypothesis.
- Force deterministic sampling (seed fixed) for a 1-hour regression job to collect consistent evidence for INFR-3245.
- For critical customers, route to baseline until fix validated.

Notes for follow-up experiments (to add to EVAL harness):
- Add synthetic test: 10k micro-perturbations with emoji / multi-byte inputs to measure off-by-one token events.
- Batch-timing test: replay sequences with varied inter-request latencies (1ms, 10ms, 100ms) to surface KV-cache race.
- Controlled sampling sweep: run temp 0.4–0.9 and measure action classification switch rate.

Rough timeline and ownership: (my dayplan)
- Today (AM): pin tokenizer & run 500-sample smoke. Tag results to INFR-3245. (owner: Jonah)
- Today (PM): kick deterministic seeding sweep (owner: Mira)
- Tomorrow: compose short one-pager for partners and CS with evidence + routing plan (owner: Jonah + Eli)

Slack snippets / copy to send to CS briefly:
- "Heads up: we see non-deterministic loss of one bullet and occasional action-switch in canary (v2.0.0) for short few-shot flows. Pinning tokenizer and running deterministic sweep now; routing baseline for affected partners until confirmed. INFR-3245."

Open questions / thinking out loud:
- Could a combination of smaller temperature + tokenization change push model to prefer shorter completions (thus truncate spot) rather than actually truncating? Need to disambiguate.
- If KV-cache misalignment occurs when connection pooling reuses slot indices, are we dropping context or returning stale KV for a different key? Trace shows both anomalies but correlation not causal yet.

TODO (short):
- [ ] Run pinned-tokenizer smoke (target 500 samples) — Jonah — due EOD
- [ ] Start deterministic seed sweep (50 seeds x 200 prompts) — Mira — due tomorrow AM
- [ ] Add emoji stress tests to EVAL harness — Eli — due next week
- [ ] Draft partner note and routing plan — Jonah/Eli — due tomorrow PM

End-of-scratch. Will paste cleaned data into confluence page when I have reproducible evidence. This file = messy working notes; use as snapshot for triage meeting.
